question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you always do?
options: a:Speed up to pass the tracks quickly.,b:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,c:Try to drive around any lowered gate.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, you should look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: If an oncoming driver has blinding high beams, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.,b:Flash your lights on and off to warn them.,c:Dim your own lights and speed up to pass quickly.
note: When confronted by blinding headlights, look right and toward the edge of the road to avoid being temporarily blinded.

question: When are road surfaces most likely to freeze quickly?
options: a:On sections shaded by trees or buildings.,b:On road segments exposed to direct sunlight.,c:On flat open stretches of highway.
note: Shaded areas freeze more quickly in cold or wet weather and are often the last parts of the road to dry, so use extra caution.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the safest action is to:
options: a:Stay inside your vehicle and wait for help.,b:Get out and walk for help immediately.,c:Lay down and sleep in your car.
note: Staying in your car makes you more likely to be found and protects you from exposure; leave only if help is very close.

question: What should be your first reaction to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Turn on your windshield wipers.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Turn on interior lights.,d:Increase your following distance only.
note: Your first response to decreased visibility should be to slow down. Adjust headlights, wipers, and following distance as needed.

question: What effect does drinking coffee have on your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.,b:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.,c:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.,d:Makes you legally sober instantly.
note: Coffee, cold showers, or other such measures do not reduce BAC or sober you up; only time does.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How long before a turn should you activate your turn signal to give others warning?
options: a:Use your signal about three to four seconds before turning.,b:Signal only as you start the turn.,c:Signal after you begin the turn.
note: Activate your turn signal about three to four seconds before making the turn to alert other road users.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It reduces your fuel efficiency only.,b:It causes a loss of engine power only.,c:It improves ventilation in the passenger compartment.,d:It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment, which is odorless and potentially fatal; fix exhaust leaks immediately.

question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, you may:
options: a:Pass only in an emergency.,b:Pass only if on an expressway.,c:Cross the broken line to pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.
note: If the broken yellow line is beside your lane, you may pass when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to move from the right lane to the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, then change lanes.,b:Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Turn on your signal while checking only the rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move to verify there is no vehicle in your blind spot. Signal every time you change lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Never cross the centerline.,b:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.,c:Move into the lane used by oncoming traffic when it is safe and legal to pass.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road requires you to enter the lane used by oncoming traffic to complete the pass, only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: Before backing out of your driveway when children are nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn before you start.,b:Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.,c:Check only your mirrors.,d:Back out slowly while watching inside the car.
note: Exit the vehicle and check behind it whenever small children are playing nearby; do not rely solely on mirrors or cameras.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect you?
options: a:It does not affect driving abilities.,b:It helps maintain driver alertness.,c:It is a distracting activity that can reduce safety.,d:It only affects drivers at night.
note: Smoking while driving can distract you by taking your eyes off the road and hands off the wheel; avoid activities that interfere with driving.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:They are decorative and optional.,b:They provide information and guidance to drivers.,c:They are only used in construction zones.,d:They indicate no-parking areas only.
note: Pavement markings guide vehicle positioning, indicate passing zones, and warn drivers of upcoming conditions; they are important for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is a true rule about passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass, and be sure no oncoming traffic is present.,b:Only check your mirrors; do not look over your shoulder.,c:Return to your lane immediately once the front bumper of the passed car is even with you.
note: Signal at least 100 feet before a lane change, check mirrors and blind spots, and ensure it is safe to pass before doing so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging into a crowded freeway, you should:
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic and yield to existing traffic.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait.,c:Enter slowly and expect freeway drivers to slow for you.
note: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate to highway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to traffic when merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in thickly settled or business districts?
options: a:10 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:30 mph.
note: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit in thickly settled areas and business districts is 30 mph; drive with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer stops you, how should you behave while waiting for the officer to approach?
options: a:Get out of the vehicle and approach the officer.,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window completely.,c:Stay in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for instructions.,d:Immediately retrieve your license and papers before the officer reaches your car.
note: Remain inside with your hands on the wheel and ask passengers to keep hands visible. Only retrieve documents when asked.

question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do about following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Keep the same following distance as dry roads.,c:Decrease your following distance.,d:Tailgate to keep flow steady.
note: On slippery surfaces give yourself extra space because stopping distances will be longer.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel.,b:It can reduce your ability to concentrate on driving.,c:It decreases your chance of an accident.,d:It improves reaction time.
note: Strong emotions and stress can lessen your concentration and impair driving performance; wait to drive if emotionally unstable.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure a safe trip home?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Take a cold shower before driving.,c:Arrange a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,d:Wait 10 minutes and drive if you feel better.
note: Only time removes alcohol from your system; the safe option is to arrange a sober ride or use other sober-transportation options.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the posted speed limit illegal?
options: a:When driving in a construction zone only.,b:Only when on rural roads.,c:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,d:When driving in heavy rain.
note: It is unlawful to drive so slowly that you impede normal traffic flow; you can be cited for unreasonably slow driving.

question: Compared with smaller vehicles, large trucks have what type of blind spots?
options: a:Smaller blind spots.,b:Larger blind spots.,c:No blind spots.,d:Only rear blind spots.
note: The bigger the vehicle, the larger its blind spots. Trucks have significant areas around them that the driver cannot see in mirrors.

question: You have a green light but pedestrians are illegally crossing against a red signal. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of them.,b:Sound your horn to clear the crosswalk.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
note: Yield to pedestrians and any vehicles in the intersection even if you have a green light; always be cautious around pedestrians.

question: Before turning the ignition on, what should you do?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers are buckled.,b:Make sure only backseat passengers have fastened seat belts.,c:Buckle only adult passengers.,d:Adjust mirrors and the radio before fastening your belt.
note: Develop a routine: before switching on the ignition, fasten your safety belt and ensure all passengers do the same.

question: Motorists should remember that large trucks:
options: a:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,b:Require less space to turn than cars.,c:Have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.
note: Trucks have significant no-zones and require greater stopping and turning distances; avoid lingering alongside them.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, you should:
options: a:Assume a door may open and use extra caution.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Brake hard and sound your horn.
note: Expect that a driver or passenger may open a door; pass with care and give extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down before you reach the exit ramp.,b:Slow down once you are on the exit ramp.,c:Keep your speed constant while on the ramp.,d:Stop at the start of the ramp and then slow down.
note: Do not decelerate suddenly on the freeway; begin slowing once you have moved onto the exit ramp and can do so safely.

question: If an approaching train is close enough or fast enough to be dangerous, you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross at your own risk if signals are off.,d:Speed up to clear the tracks before it arrives.
note: If a train is near enough or moving quickly, do not cross the tracks; wait until it has safely passed and all warning devices indicate it is clear.

question: When driving in bad weather you should:
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Increase speed to reach your destination sooner.
note: On wet or slippery roads increase following distance to allow more stopping time.

question: If you're waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and oncoming traffic blocks your view, you should:
options: a:Wave oncoming drivers to let you go.,b:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before turning.,c:Accelerate rapidly as soon as the first lane clears.
note: Never start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes you must cross are clear and the turn can be made safely.

question: Which traffic signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A steady green light.,d:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow and proceed with caution; a flashing red means stop.

question: When it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance.,b:Maintain normal following distance and drive as usual.,c:Speed up to get to your destination sooner.
note: In sleet or snow, keep windshield and mirrors clear and allow extra space between you and the vehicle ahead because stopping distances increase on slippery roads.

question: When stopped by police for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must the driver produce?
options: a:Proof of insurance only.,b:The driver's license.,c:Proof of vehicle registration only.
note: When stopped, the driver must be prepared to produce their license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance; carrying all three is required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the other vehicle.,b:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Enter the intersection and force the other vehicle to stop.,d:Honk to assert your right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed only when safe.

question: If you are involved in a crash, what is your first responsibility at the scene?
options: a:Stop your vehicle immediately and remain at the scene.,b:Immediately leave the scene and report later.,c:Drive to the nearest police station before helping.,d:Continue driving if damage appears minor.
note: If involved in a crash you must stop. Move out of traffic if possible, call for help, and provide assistance without moving seriously injured people unless necessary.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest rule when vehicles are approaching a crosswalk?
options: a:Always insist on your right-of-way and step into traffic.,b:Never enter a street or crosswalk while vehicles are approaching closely.,c:Assume drivers will always stop for you.,d:Cross at any point regardless of vehicle distance.
note: Pedestrians should not step into a crosswalk when vehicles are approaching too closely to stop safely; even with right-of-way, allow vehicles time to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has multiple lanes going your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.,b:Turn into the middle lane.,c:Turn into the lane closest to your original lane.,d:Turn and immediately change into any lane you prefer.
note: When turning onto a street with more than one lane in the same direction, turn into the lane closest to the one you came from and do not change lanes during the turn.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your front wheels away from the curb.,b:Keep the front wheels straight ahead.,c:Keep the rear tires tight against the curb.
note: Facing uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving.,b:Excessive speed for conditions.,c:Following other vehicles too closely.,d:All of the above.
note: Inattentive driving, driving too fast for conditions, and tailgating are frequent causes of collisions.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator suddenly sticks open while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off the ignition while steering to a safe area, apply brakes, and pull off the road.,b:Slam on your brakes and jump out.,c:Blow your horn continuously and stay in the lane.,d:Shift into neutral and keep driving at speed until help arrives.
note: If the accelerator sticks, ease off the gas, shift to neutral, carefully turn off the ignition once safe to stop the engine, and brake to a safe area; avoid locking the steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:Whoever is turning has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,d:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: When driving near large trucks, what should other drivers account for?
options: a:That large vehicles stop much sooner than cars.,b:That large vehicles can see everything behind them.,c:That trucks always yield to smaller vehicles.,d:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
note: Large vehicles require more distance to stop and have bigger blind spots; give them space and avoid lingering where the trucker cannot see you.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by easing off the gas, then brake gently.,c:Maintain current speed and keep steering locked.,d:Turn sharply toward the shoulder and brake hard.
note: Keep the vehicle headed straight, ease off the gas without braking until you are in control, then brake gently and pull safely off the road.

question: Roads become especially slippery when:
options: a:Rain first begins for the initial 10 to 15 minutes.,b:It has been raining for several hours.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Pavement is most slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of rain as oil on the surface mixes with water.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed immediately once the bus starts moving.,b:Watch carefully for children walking along the side of the road.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.
note: After a school bus extends its stop arm and children are unloading, watch for children who may walk into the roadway and proceed only when it is safe.

question: An 'End school zone' sign indicates:
options: a:The end of the reduced speed school zone.,b:The start of a 20 mph zone.,c:That pedestrians are more likely to be present.
note: The 'End school zone' sign marks the end of the reduced school speed zone.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:All occupants of the vehicle.,b:Only the driver.,c:Passengers only on long trips.
note: Every occupant should wear a seat belt; unbelted passengers can become projectiles in a crash.

question: Alcohol affects driving by:
options: a:Slowing reflexes and reaction time.,b:Waking you up and sharpening reflexes.,c:Having no effect at low doses.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity and reduces skills needed for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway you must:
options: a:Stop and proceed only when no vehicles or pedestrians are approaching.,b:Honk to alert others and then go.,c:Drive slowly so others will get out of your way.
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway and yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians.

question: During winter weather, how do overpasses and bridges compare to other roadways?
options: a:They are affected exactly the same as other roadways.,b:They thaw out before the rest of the roads.,c:They are always safer to drive on.,d:They can freeze before and remain icy longer than other road surfaces.
note: Bridges and overpasses are exposed to air on all sides and may ice over sooner and remain icy longer than regular road surfaces.

question: What effect does taking drugs along with alcohol have on driving risk?
options: a:No change in risk.,b:Less dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:Increases the risk of causing a crash.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs, including legal medications, increases impairment and the risk of being involved in a crash.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down and continue driving.,c:Turn on your hazard flashers and keep going.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with siren or lights, you must pull to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Re-enter your lane within ten feet of the passed vehicle.,b:Honk your horn repeatedly then pass.,c:Check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, and only re-enter the lane when you can see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror.
note: Before passing, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and re-enter only when you can see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When using a roundabout, which action is required?
options: a:Yield to entering traffic.,b:Drive in a clockwise direction around the central island.,c:Stop in the center before exiting.,d:Enter from the right, yielding to traffic already in the roundabout.
note: Roundabouts flow counterclockwise; drivers entering must yield to traffic already circulating and follow the circle to their exit.

question: You must pull to the road edge and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights:
options: a:Regardless of whether it is approaching from behind or facing you.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is coming toward you from the opposite direction.
note: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop for emergency vehicles with flashing lights regardless of direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Sharply toward the curb.,b:Slightly to the right.,c:Parallel to the curb with wheels straight.,d:Sharply away from the curb.
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it begins to move.

question: How must drivers treat pedestrians on the roadway?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian notices their vehicle.,b:Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is wrong.,c:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must do everything they can to avoid striking pedestrians. Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians even if they are not strictly obeying rules.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Before stopping, only check your blind spots.,b:Drive in the center of the lane always.,c:Brake late and hard to surprise tailgaters.,d:Avoid sudden stops and allow extra following distance.
note: Release the gas early to allow the vehicle to slow, signal and brake smoothly to give drivers behind you time to react.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what is the first action you should take?
options: a:Apply firm continuous pressure to the brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Engage the parking brake.
note: To slow on slippery surfaces, first lift your foot off the accelerator. If more slowing is needed, gently apply steady pressure to the brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Stop and reverse into the correct lane.,d:Continue to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.
note: Do not make last-minute or unsafe turns; proceed to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

question: What single action most effectively reduces your risk of serious injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Driving at speed limits above posted values.,b:Staying in the right lane.,c:Driving only on weekdays.,d:Wearing your seat belt.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective thing you can do to lower the risk of death or serious injury in a crash.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Only marijuana.,c:Illegal drugs as well as prescription and over-the-counter medications.
note: Many substances, including illegal drugs and legal prescription or OTC medications, can impair your ability to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to reach the exit.,b:Make a U-turn on the interstate.,c:Continue to the next exit and exit there.,d:Stop in the lane and back up.
note: Do not make unsafe last-minute maneuvers; continue to the next exit and re-route from there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these must you obey over the others?
options: a:A steady red traffic light.,b:A police officer directing traffic.,c:A stop sign.
note: Directions from authorized traffic officers take precedence over traffic signals, signs, and pavement markings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.,b:Only signal if other vehicles are nearby.,c:Signal only at night.
note: Always use your turn signals when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb to alert other road users.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pennant-shaped signs, placed on the left side of the road, typically indicate no passing zones.

question: What characteristic defines a good defensive driver?
options: a:Travels at a constant slow speed at all times.,b:Looks ahead for the actions of other drivers and anticipates hazards.,c:Relies only on other drivers to behave properly.,d:Always follows the vehicle directly in front of them closely.
note: A defensive driver looks for and anticipates the actions of others, allowing time to react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:Never under any circumstances.,b:To pass a slow vehicle when there's no oncoming traffic.,c:To turn into or out of a driveway or make a permitted left turn.
note: Double solid lines prohibit passing; crossing is allowed for permitted left turns into or from driveways or roadways.

question: What does a green arrow signal mean?
options: a:It only applies to one-way streets.,b:Traffic may proceed and must turn in the direction of the arrow.,c:You may proceed only if a circular green light is also showing.
note: A green arrow allows traffic in the indicated lane to proceed and requires drivers to turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

question: To avoid driving unsafely due to health, what should you do?
options: a:Rely on occasional rest instead of medical checks.,b:Always drive regardless of physical condition.,c:Ignore medication warnings if you feel fine.,d:Keep fit, know how medicines affect you, and drive within your limitations.
note: Drivers should be aware of their physical limits, maintain health, and understand how medications or conditions affect driving ability.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:Only when pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:When changing lanes, turning, or pulling toward/away from a curb.,c:Only when turning left or right.,d:Only if your mirrors show nothing.
note: Always check blind spots by glancing over your shoulder any time you intend to change the vehicle's position: turning, changing lanes, or leaving/approaching a curb.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, how should you re-enter the road?
options: a:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,b:Stop on the shoulder and wait for help.,c:Slow down, regain control, and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,d:Speed up and swerve back onto the pavement.
note: Reduce speed without braking hard, check traffic, and carefully steer back onto the roadway when it is safe to do so.

question: A solid red arrow displayed by a traffic signal means:
options: a:A driver may proceed slowly in the arrow's direction.,b:It only applies to pedestrians.,c:The same as a yellow arrow.,d:Traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction.
note: A steady red arrow has the same effect as a circular red light for that lane: you must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction until it changes.

question: When driving on slick roads, how should you handle turns?
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly to avoid puddles.,c:Accelerate through the turn to maintain momentum.
note: Approach and negotiate turns more slowly on slippery roads to reduce the risk of skidding or losing control.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light require you to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,b:Slow and proceed with caution in the arrow's direction.,c:Stop and then proceed when clear even if the arrow stays red.,d:Make the turn if no other traffic is present.
note: A red arrow means stop for the arrow indication and remain stopped until it changes to green or a green arrow.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving typically:
options: a:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or vehicle operation.,b:Are always aware of the risks they're taking.,c:Drive better because they are more careful.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time; it never makes driving safer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, who must yield?
options: a:Drivers already on the interstate always yield.,b:The entering driver should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,c:The entering driver may force their way into traffic.,d:No one needs to yield on freeways.
note: Drivers merging from an entrance or acceleration ramp should yield to traffic already on the interstate and merge safely when a gap is available.

question: Signs that indicate areas of public recreation are what color?
options: a:Brown.,b:Green.,c:Red.
note: Brown signs mark cultural, historical, and recreational areas and attractions.

question: The effect of being awake for many hours on your driving ability is similar to:
options: a:The effect of alcohol on driving ability.,b:The effect of taking amphetamines.,c:The effect of anger on driving.,d:The effect of reading before driving.
note: Fatigue impairs driving in a manner comparable to alcohol: long periods awake can produce impairment similar to a measurable BAC.

question: At a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Always stop no matter what.,b:Accelerate to clear the tracks quickly.,c:Prepare to yield and look both ways for trains before crossing.,d:Shift gears while crossing to avoid stalling.
note: When there are no active warnings, slow, look both ways, and be prepared to stop for any approaching train; never start across unless you can clear the tracks completely.

question: Which of the following is illegal for passengers in a moving motor vehicle?
options: a:Using a cell phone.,b:Sleeping.,c:Having an opened alcohol container.
note: It is unlawful for anyone to possess or drink from an open alcohol container in a motor vehicle on a public road.

question: If you must drive in fog, you should:
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights only.,b:Turn on low beam headlights (not high beams).,c:Drive at the maximum posted speed.
note: Use low beams and fog lights if available; high beams reduce visibility by reflecting off fog.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Driving aggressively to control the road.,b:Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.,c:Driving against the traffic to avoid others.
note: Defensive driving means altering your driving to fit conditions, anticipating hazards, and using safe strategies to avoid crashes.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold the brake pedal down firmly.,b:Firmly pump the brakes repeatedly.,c:Tap the brakes lightly.
note: If your vehicle lacks ABS, the best method in an emergency is to pump the brakes firmly to stop quickly while retaining some steering control.

question: How can you avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Honk your horn before changing lanes.,b:Turn your head quickly to check the blind spot before moving.,c:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,d:Assume mirrors are always enough.
note: Before changing lanes or turning, glance over your shoulder toward the direction of travel to check blind spots; do not rely only on mirrors.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane indicate a crosswalk. As a driver, what must you do?
options: a:Speed through if you do not see pedestrians.,b:Only stop if the crosswalk is unmarked.,c:Assume pedestrians yield to vehicles.,d:Always stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk and yield the right-of-way.
note: Marked crosswalks indicate where pedestrians may cross; vehicles must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Check mirrors and look over your shoulder to verify there is no vehicle in your blind spot.,b:Reduce your speed dramatically.,c:Sound your horn as a signal.
note: Check rearview and side mirrors and glance over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear before changing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:Both vehicles should wave at each other to communicate.
note: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:
options: a:Yield only to traffic on your left.,b:Always come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersecting roadway.
note: A yield sign requires you to slow and give right-of-way to other traffic or pedestrians as needed.

question: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or lights, you should:
options: a:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.,b:Turn your radio up so you can hear trains better.,c:Wait for a flagger to tell you to cross.
note: Always approach such crossings cautiously and only cross when certain no trains are approaching from either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper sequence when changing lanes?
options: a:Rely solely on your mirrors and move over.,b:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot by looking over your shoulder, then change lanes.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and move only when it is safe.

question: Which actions will help you drive more safely at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance and ensure your headlights are working properly.,b:Drive only if you are very tired.,c:Turn off your headlights when there is oncoming traffic.,d:Use high beams at all times for the best visibility.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance, avoid driving if tired, and make sure headlights and signals work properly.

question: When is it legal to cross a dashed white lane line?
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:Never.,d:Only if following a motorcycle.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Keep a steady pace and stay there.,c:Stay in the blind spot to prevent lane changes.
note: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot. Move forward or fall back until you are visible in the other driver's mirrors.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, how should you proceed?
options: a:Try to squeeze between them by splitting the difference.,b:Pull onto the shoulder to pass both at once.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist when safe.
note: When multiple hazards exist, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass, then safely pass the bicyclist giving ample space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to turn left at an intersection where the light is green but heavy oncoming traffic prevents it. You should:
options: a:Wait for a safe gap in oncoming traffic before turning; you may enter the intersection to prepare if the light is green.,b:Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.,c:Use the next intersection instead always.
note: You may move into the intersection to prepare for a left turn on a green light but only complete the turn when all lanes you must cross are clear.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to a:
options: a:Stop sign.,b:Yield sign.,c:Solid red light without stopping required.,d:No entry sign.
note: A flashing red traffic signal requires a full stop, like a stop sign, then proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Higher speed always improves safety.,b:Speeding is never dangerous if you are an experienced driver.,c:Speed has no effect on crash severity.,d:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
note: Both excessive speed and driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous. Speed affects crash severity and driver control.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what is true about turning?
options: a:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn and must proceed straight only.,c:You keep the exclusive right-of-way to turn.
note: When the arrow ends and the light is solid green, turning is allowed but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: Which of the following helps a person overcome the influence of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Tomato juice and lime.,b:Hot coffee.,c:Fresh air.,d:Only the passage of time.
note: No remedy will sober someone quickly; only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do on a two-lane road?
options: a:Stop immediately in your lane.,b:Drive as far to the right as is safe and stop.,c:Proceed slowly and allow it to pass on your left.
note: On a two-lane or undivided highway, move as near as possible to the right side and stop to yield to the emergency vehicle.

question: Which restraints are most effective in a crash?
options: a:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag used together.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Only a lap belt.
note: Seat belts combined with airbags provide the best protection; belts must be worn to get full benefit from airbags.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, after one train passes you should:
options: a:Look for another train on the other track before crossing.,b:Always stop and call authorities.,c:Assume it is safe to proceed immediately.
note: After one train passes, another may be approaching on the adjacent track—ensure both tracks are clear before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:
options: a:You can see far enough ahead to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:You are able to clearly see the road ahead only a short distance.,c:Your vehicle is the fastest on the road.
note: You must be able to see the road ahead sufficiently to pass and return to your lane before encountering oncoming traffic.

question: When a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon shows two flashing red lights, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding with caution.,b:Slow and proceed if clear.,c:Ignore it unless pedestrians are visible.
note: A PHB displaying two flashing red lights requires drivers to stop, then proceed only when safe.

question: If you approach railroad crossing with signals flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and look for a train, at least 15 feet from the nearest rail.,b:Slow down and proceed if you do not see a train.,c:Speed up to beat the train.
note: When signals at a railroad crossing are flashing, you must stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until it is safe to cross.

question: What are the colors of highway guide signs that show distances to exits and destinations?
options: a:Black background with white letters.,b:Yellow background with black letters.,c:Red background with white letters.,d:Green background with white letters.
note: Destination and distance guide signs on highways are green with white letters or symbols to direct drivers to exits and locations.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that what will soon follow?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A steady green light.,c:A steady red light.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn steady red, so prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a “Reduced speed, 35 mph” sign mean?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at that sign.,b:The new speed begins at the next sign.,c:You have plenty of time to slow down after passing the sign.,d:The reduction is only a suggestion.
note: A posted reduced speed sign indicates the new speed limit begins at the sign and must be obeyed from that point.

question: When you encounter a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to alert the pedestrian and proceed.,b:Assume they will avoid your vehicle.,c:Take the right-of-way and proceed.,d:Slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop.
note: Slow and yield to blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog; be ready to stop to prevent harm.

question: At a railroad crossing where you do not see or hear a train, when must you stop?
options: a:Only during nighttime hours.,b:Only when a train is visible.,c:If you are towing a trailer only.,d:If a stop sign is posted or if crossing lights are flashing or a gate is lowered.
note: You must stop at railroad crossings when a stop sign is posted, warning lights are flashing, crossing gates are lowered, a flagger signals you, or a train is so close it is hazardous to cross.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:A pedestrian lane.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,d:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Solid white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and indicate that lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multi-lane road, when you see a 'Merging traffic' sign you should:
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by moving over if safe and possible.,b:Always keep your current speed and position.,c:Honk at incoming drivers to warn them off.
note: When multiple lanes exist, give space to merging vehicles; change lanes if safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are stopped in a line and the vehicles ahead move through a stop sign. If no cross traffic is present, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,b:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before moving on.,c:Slowly roll through the stop sign to maintain traffic flow.,d:Honk to warn pedestrians before moving.
note: Even if traffic ahead has cleared the intersection, you must bring your vehicle to a complete stop at the stop sign or line before proceeding.

question: What is the best way to handle a driver who is following you too closely?
options: a:Speed up to increase the gap between you and the tailgater.,b:Slam on your brakes to make them fall back.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow to encourage them to pass.
note: If another car is following you too closely, move to another lane when safe or slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass. Avoid sudden braking.

question: For drivers age 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of:
options: a:0.08 percent or higher.,b:0.05 percent or higher.,c:0.02 percent or higher.
note: Drivers age 21+ may not operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or greater. Driving under the influence is both illegal and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit represents:
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:The suggested safe speed under all conditions.,c:The speed you must always travel regardless of conditions.
note: Speed limits represent the maximum/minimum legal speed under normal conditions; adjust lower when conditions demand.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When do you have the right-of-way while turning left at a signal?
options: a:When facing a solid green light.,b:When facing a flashing yellow light.,c:When facing a green arrow pointing left.,d:When oncoming traffic is turning right.
note: A steady green arrow gives protected turn movement; oncoming traffic should be stopped for the arrow direction.

question: To prepare for anything ahead on the road, you should:
options: a:Continually scan the entire roadway and roadsides.,b:Stare straight ahead at the center of the road only.,c:Keep your left foot lightly on the brake.,d:Focus only on the vehicle directly ahead of you.
note: Search and identify possible problems by scanning far ahead and to the sides of the road to allow time to react safely.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in front of your vehicle.,b:Only to the left and right.,c:On all sides of the vehicle.,d:Only behind the vehicle.
note: Maintain a cushion of space on all sides of your vehicle so you have room to react to hazards and avoid collisions.

question: When a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon shows two solid red lights, what must drivers do?
options: a:Proceed with caution without stopping.,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped for pedestrians.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: A Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon displaying two steady red lights requires drivers to stop and remain stopped for pedestrians crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you prepare to make a left turn, what should you be doing?
options: a:Signal in advance, slow gradually, and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Speed up to beat oncoming traffic.,c:Make the turn from the far right lane.,d:Ignore pedestrians if you have a green light.
note: Signal three to five seconds before turning, slow gradually while checking mirrors, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and then turn when safe.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, what actions should you take?
options: a:Drive cautiously, reduce speed, and use low beam headlights.,b:Use high beam headlights to better see ahead.,c:Drive at normal speed if traffic is light.,d:Turn off all lights to reduce glare.
note: In fog, lower your speed, drive with caution, and use low beams (not high beams) to improve visibility of the road ahead.

question: If another vehicle is about to collide with you, you should:
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Do nothing and hope they avoid you.,c:Sound your horn to warn the other driver and pedestrians.
note: Use your horn to warn others of imminent danger if it may prevent a collision.

question: If an aggressive driver is following you closely and acting hostile, what should you do?
options: a:Brake-check them to teach a lesson.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Try to get out of their way and avoid confrontation.,d:Speed up to challenge them.
note: If confronted by an aggressive driver, avoid escalation: move out of the way, don't make eye contact, and call authorities if needed.

question: When should you reduce your speed when approaching a curve in the road?
options: a:Only if you feel uncomfortable.,b:After you have entered the curve.,c:Before you enter the curve.,d:Only if another car is behind you.
note: Slow down before entering a curve so you will not need to brake while turning; braking in a curve can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Just before you begin to change lanes to pass.,b:Only if the vehicle ahead signals.,c:After you have already started the pass.,d:Signal early enough that other drivers understand your intention.
note: Signal early enough to notify other drivers of your intentions before you begin the passing maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it unsafe to make a U-turn?
options: a:At the crest of a hill or near a curve because visibility is limited.,b:In the middle of an intersection if traffic is clear.,c:Anywhere drivers can see you for 500 feet in both directions.
note: Do not make U-turns at the crest of a hill, near a curve, or any place where visibility is limited; drivers must be able to see 500 feet in both directions.

question: What does a diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Warning of existing or possible hazards ahead.,b:Alerts drivers to school zones.,c:Indicates recreational areas.,d:Shows route information.
note: Diamond-shaped signs (usually yellow or orange) warn drivers of potential hazards or changes in the roadway ahead.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn on your headlights (low beams).,b:Use only your parking lights.,c:Do not turn on any lights.
note: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights and use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or 500 feet of one you are following.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels run off the pavement, what is the correct action?
options: a:Accelerate and turn sharply back onto the road.,b:Ease off the accelerator, steer parallel to the roadway, slow down, then carefully steer back on when safe.,c:Stop immediately on the shoulder.
note: If your wheels leave the pavement, don't panic. Take your foot off the gas, steer parallel to the road, slow down, and then return to the pavement with a small, controlled turn when safe.

question: Which statement about sudden weather changes is true?
options: a:There is no need to change driving style in rain or fog.,b:You should ignore vehicles behind you in bad weather.,c:A sudden change in weather requires you to adjust your driving.
note: If the weather changes suddenly, adjust speed and driving style accordingly, and be especially aware of vehicles behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.,b:Move as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.,c:Creep into the intersection to get a better view.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it without blocking cross traffic; wait until traffic ahead clears.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Look for a way around a lowered gate.,b:Drive faster to beat an approaching train.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,d:Ignore it if no signals are present.
note: Railroad warning signs indicate a crossing ahead; be ready to slow or stop for approaching trains and never go around lowered gates.

question: What driving behavior can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Accelerating quickly from a stop.,b:Sitting idling in your driveway.,c:Slowing down and coasting to avoid unnecessary stops.,d:Frequent hard braking to control speed.
note: Avoiding rapid acceleration and unnecessary stops, and anticipating traffic to slow gradually, helps improve fuel economy.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines painted across lanes) located?
options: a:In curves and on hills only.,b:Only on one-way streets.,c:Next to churches and schools only.,d:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines mark the exact location where a vehicle must stop at an intersection or pedestrian crosswalk.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, you should glance:
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:Only at the rearview mirror.,c:At your side mirror.,d:Over your left shoulder.
note: To verify your blind spot on the side you intend to move toward, glance over that shoulder rather than relying solely on mirrors.

question: What does an orange-colored traffic sign usually indicate?
options: a:A hospital zone ahead.,b:A railroad crossing ahead.,c:A school zone ahead.,d:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.
note: Orange signs warn of highway construction, maintenance activities, or emergency operations and require heightened caution.

question: When is it permissible to cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:To pass slower traffic at any time.,b:Only when making a left turn into a driveway or side street.,c:During daytime hours only.,d:Whenever the lane beside you is clear.
note: Solid yellow lines should not be crossed for passing; you may cross a solid yellow only when turning left into or from a driveway, alley, or private road.

question: A flashing yellow arrow for left turns indicates:
options: a:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You must come to a complete stop before turning.,c:You should merge into the lane in the arrow's direction without yielding.
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns but requires yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians first.

question: If a vehicle with ABS begins to lose traction on a slippery road, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer out of danger.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Press and hold the accelerator.
note: If your vehicle has ABS, press hard and hold the brake while steering; ABS will automatically modulate the braking.

question: What is a vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:The area directly behind your vehicle.,b:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,c:The area visible in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in mirrors without turning your head. Check them by glancing over your shoulder.

question: What risks do worn or bald tires pose?
options: a:They can increase your stopping distance.,b:They improve fuel efficiency.,c:They make steering more precise.,d:They reduce the chance of hydroplaning.
note: Tires with inadequate tread can increase stopping distance, make turning more difficult, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:The full width of a lane, the same as other vehicles.,b:Only the bicycle lane.,c:Half the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as other motor vehicles and should be given full-lane respect.

question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter traffic after stopping, you must:
options: a:Yield to the transit vehicle to allow it to re-enter safely.,b:Honk to warn the driver.,c:Speed up and pass the bus.
note: Yield, change lanes, slow, or stop to let a transit bus safely merge back into traffic after passenger loading.

question: What do your vehicle's brake lights communicate to other drivers?
options: a:You are about to make a turn.,b:You are changing lanes.,c:You are slowing down or stopping.,d:Your parking brake is engaged.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing or stopping; keep them in working order for safety.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Overcorrect and turn the wheel hard away from the skid.,b:Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm and steer gently in the direction of the skid until you regain control.

question: Green pavement markings typically indicate:
options: a:Emergency-only lanes.,b:HOV lanes exclusively.,c:Areas with potential conflicts between bicycles and motor vehicles.
note: Green pavement highlights areas with possible vehicle-bicycle conflicts; watch closely for bicyclists.

question: You see the driver ahead driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:
options: a:Give that vehicle extra space because the driver may be inattentive.,b:Follow their example.,c:Speed up to pass immediately.
note: Distracted drivers have reduced safety margins; allow extra space to reduce crash risk.

question: How far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph need to stop?
options: a:About 50 feet.,b:About 125 feet.,c:Up to 400 feet.
note: Heavily loaded tractor-trailers require much greater stopping distances than passenger cars; at 55 mph they can need almost 400 feet to stop.

question: To reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road ahead.,b:Keep looking straight into the oncoming headlights.,c:Look over your shoulder.
note: If oncoming drivers do not dim their lights, keep your eyes on the right side of the road ahead. Do not stare directly at oncoming headlights to avoid temporary blindness.

question: Which of the following is an effect of alcohol on driving?
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Improved coordination.,c:Faster judgment.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:Never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger airbag.,b:An airbag is harmless to infants and small children.,c:Children age 12 and under should always ride in the front seat.,d:Seat belts are optional for backseat passengers.
note: Children 12 and under should ride properly restrained in the rear seat; never place a rear-facing infant seat where an active passenger airbag is present.

question: When following a motorcycle, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:Two seconds.,b:Three seconds.,c:Four seconds.,d:One second.
note: Increase your following distance to at least four seconds when following a motorcycle to allow extra time to react if the rider falls or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center two-way left-turn lane, what maneuvers are permitted?
options: a:You may make left turns from either direction.,b:You may use it for passing slow traffic.,c:You may drive through it as a through lane.,d:You may make U-turns at any time.
note: A center two-way left-turn lane is reserved for left turns from either direction; it is not for passing or through travel.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and driving?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.,d:Only dangerous for inexperienced drivers.
note: Driving under the influence is a serious safety problem; alcohol impairs the ability to drive safely for anyone.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed of your vehicle.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The condition of the pavement.,d:All of the above.
note: Stopping distance is influenced by speed, vehicle weight, weather and visibility, brakes and tire condition, and the roadway surface.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching from any direction, what action is required?
options: a:Slow down and remain in your lane.,b:Keep driving but do not block intersections.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop until it has passed.,d:Immediately back up to clear the way.
note: Upon seeing or hearing an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, pull to the right side of the road and stop until it passes or you are directed otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Whenever conditions make driving less than perfect, such as rain or poor visibility.,b:Only when you see a police car.,c:Only when entering a highway with other cars.
note: Drive below the posted speed limit whenever road, weather, or visibility conditions make higher speeds unsafe.

question: A stop sign has what shape?
options: a:Octagon.,b:Circle.,c:Rectangle.
note: Only stop signs are eight-sided (octagonal); they require a complete stop.

question: When it starts to rain while you're driving, you should:
options: a:Slow down, turn on headlights, and if visibility is poor pull off safely.,b:Increase speed to get home faster.,c:Drive at the posted maximum speed limit.
note: Reduce speed when rain reduces visibility or traction; use headlights and pull over if conditions worsen.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Only when a police officer is present.,b:At an intersection with a stop sign, at a red light, or when ordered by a traffic officer.,c:Only when other vehicles are present.,d:Never unless there is an emergency.
note: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,b:You won't be able to see their turn signals.,c:It makes traffic flow slower.
note: Following too closely reduces stopping time and increases risk of rear-end collisions.

question: Fluorescent yellow-green road signs are used to warn drivers about which situation?
options: a:Hospital locations.,b:Speed limits.,c:School zones and pedestrian or bicycle warnings.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: Fluorescent yellow-green is the standard background for pedestrian, bicycle, and school warning signs; use extra caution when you see them.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, you should:
options: a:Shift into park immediately.,b:Reach down and try to pull up the pedal while continuing to steer.,c:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake, then pull off safely and turn off the engine.
note: Keep control, shift to neutral, brake steadily, and exit the roadway safely before turning off the engine.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,c:A circular green sign.,d:A reflective orange triangle (slow-moving vehicle emblem).
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle, used on vehicles that cannot travel faster than about 25 mph.

question: If a driver is turning while a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield.,b:The driver turning must yield to the pedestrian.,c:Whoever started moving last must yield.,d:The driver may proceed if turning quickly.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections or crosswalks, even if there is no traffic signal.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on each of the following, except:
options: a:Your body weight.,b:The type of alcoholic beverage (this does not affect BAC).,c:How much time passes between drinks.
note: BAC depends on how much you drink, your weight, and time between drinks; the beverage type does not change BAC.

question: Compared to daytime driving, nighttime driving is generally:
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because visibility is reduced, glare can blind drivers, and others on the road may be fatigued or impaired.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:The center of the road.,b:The left side of the road.,c:The right side of the road.,d:Directly at the headlights.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams while maintaining your lane position.

question: Tailgating is:
options: a:Illegal and a common cause of rear-end crashes.,b:Only an inconvenience.,c:The fastest way to reach your destination.
note: Never tailgate; it is illegal in many places and greatly increases rear-end collision risk.

question: When approaching a flashing yellow light, drivers should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop every time.,c:Increase speed to get through quickly.
note: A flashing yellow warns of a potential hazard—slow and proceed carefully.

question: Which type of sign warns you about hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs advise drivers of potentially hazardous conditions ahead; obey them to avoid accidents.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions.,b:Drivers may pass or change lanes when it is safe.,c:Drivers may not pass.,d:A pedestrian crossing.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: If your wheels run off the edge of the pavement, what is the safest way to return to the road?
options: a:Jerk the steering wheel to quickly slam back onto the pavement.,b:Increase speed and abruptly steer back onto the road.,c:Gently brake, slow down, and steer gradually back onto the pavement when safe.,d:Slam on the brakes and stop in the shoulder.
note: Remain calm, gently slow down while off the pavement, and when at a safe speed steer back onto the road; avoid sudden turns or braking.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, you should:
options: a:Take time to calm down and focus before driving.,b:Drive quickly to get the trip over with.,c:Be fine to drive—emotions don't affect driving.
note: Strong emotions distract your attention; delay driving until you can focus on the road.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Merging traffic only.,c:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,d:Come to a full stop before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns drivers to slow down and proceed with caution; it does not require a full stop.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,b:When exiting an expressway.,c:When following a motorcycle in good weather.
note: Increase following distance when behind large vehicles that block your vision, in bad weather, heavy traffic, or when a motorcycle or bicycle is ahead.

question: Which action helps prevent crashes by communicating with other road users?
options: a:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your vehicle.,b:Drive only on side streets to avoid interactions.,c:Use your signals and horn when appropriate.
note: Crashes often happen when road users behave unpredictably; communicate with signals, brake lights, and horn when necessary to make your intentions clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When you are in a school zone.,b:If it requires driving off the pavement, c:On a narrow bridge.,c:If the vehicle ahead is waiting to make a left turn and there is a sufficient lane on the right.
note: You may pass on the right when a vehicle is turning left and there is a safe, legal lane to pass in; do not drive off the pavement to pass.

question: A traffic signal showing a green arrow plus a red light means:
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light to move in any direction.,b:You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.,c:You may only drive straight ahead.
note: A green arrow with a red light allows movement only in the arrow's direction when the intersection is clear.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles on the road?
options: a:Motorcycles always stop more quickly than cars.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers.,c:Motorcyclists rarely use helmets.,d:Motorcycles are more difficult to see than cars.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots; it is harder to judge their distance and speed, so take extra care around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane furthest from your original lane.,b:Into the lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Any lane that appears clear.,d:The center lane regardless of markings.
note: When turning onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from unless markings indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where must your vehicle be positioned when making a right turn?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Near the left side of the street.,c:As close as possible to the right side of the street.
note: When preparing for a right turn, position your vehicle as far to the right as possible. Do not cut across lanes to make the turn.

question: What is the best way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires properly maintained and reduce speed when roads are wet.,b:Use cruise control on wet roads.,c:Drive faster to get through puddles quickly.,d:Inflate tires to the maximum pressure regardless of conditions.
note: Proper tire maintenance and reducing speed on wet roads help prevent hydroplaning; do not use cruise control in such conditions.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Never; you have the right-of-way.,b:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.,c:Only when other vehicles yield first.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights or sirens by pulling to the right and stopping.

question: When a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, the driver is indicating:
options: a:An intention to stop or slow.,b:An intention to turn left.,c:An intention to turn right.
note: A left arm extended down signals a stop or slowing; adjust your driving accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to which road users?
options: a:Vehicles already in the roundabout, bicyclists, and pedestrians.,b:Only pedestrians.,c:Only vehicles entering from the left.,d:Only emergency vehicles.
note: Yield to all users already in the roundabout—vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians—before entering safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb is:
options: a:A good driving habit and required by law.,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:Required during the maneuver but not before it.,d:Only necessary during daylight hours.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes or turning. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?
options: a:They are blind and may not see or hear your vehicle.,b:They are always accompanied by a guide dog that obeys traffic.,c:They must yield to vehicles.,d:They cannot enter crosswalks.
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog are blind or visually impaired; you must yield and be prepared to stop to avoid injury.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The alcohol cancels the drug's effects.,b:There will never be any interaction.,c:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.,d:The combination is always safe.
note: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairment and unpredictably increase dangerous effects.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without signals, what should you do?
options: a:Always bring your vehicle to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop after checking both directions for trains.,c:Assume all railroad crossings have signals and proceed normally.
note: When approaching an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary. Never assume there are signals.

question: What is the only reliable way to lower your BAC?
options: a:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee to sober up.,c:Exercise to speed up alcohol metabolism.
note: Only time reduces BAC; coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not lower blood alcohol concentration.

question: When stopped in line of traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, what should you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and can proceed without checking.,b:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,c:There is enough space ahead so your vehicle can clear the tracks without stopping.
note: Ensure there is enough room to fully cross the tracks before entering; never stop on the tracks or attempt to pass other vehicles there.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.,b:Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.,c:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and drive to a safe area before stopping.,d:Steer sharply to the side and stop immediately in the lane.
note: Power steering loss makes steering heavier; slow down, steer carefully, and move to a safe area before stopping.

question: How should you treat traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:You must follow them only when other traffic is present.,b:They are merely suggestions.,c:They only apply to commercial vehicles.,d:They must always be obeyed.
note: Traffic devices—signs, signals, pavement markings—control flow and safety; you must obey them at all times.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be difficult to see in traffic.,b:They obey different traffic laws.,c:They always have the legal right-of-way.
note: Smaller road users can be harder to spot and may move unpredictably, so be extra vigilant to avoid collisions.

question: If you are upset or angry before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn the radio loud to forget about it.,b:Drive fast on the highway to release tension.,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
note: If you are emotionally upset, allow yourself time to cool off before driving. Driving while angry or distracted is dangerous.

question: What is the consequence of refusing an alcohol analysis test when suspected of OUI in Massachusetts?
options: a:There are no consequences for refusal.,b:You get a warning only.,c:Refusal is recommended.,d:Your driver's license will be suspended.
note: In Massachusetts implied consent law means refusing a required alcohol or controlled substance test will result in administrative suspension of driving privileges.

question: In rainy driving conditions which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights when driving in rain, fog, or snow to improve visibility without creating glare for others.

question: Which of these is important when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Signal your intentions in advance.,b:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,c:Make sure the lane is clear before moving.,d:All of the above.
note: Always signal ahead of a lane change, check mirrors and blind spots, and confirm the lane is clear before you move.

question: Being distracted while driving:
options: a:Usually causes drivers to drive faster.,b:Usually causes slower reactions to hazards.,c:Is not dangerous.
note: Any distracting activity slows a driver's reaction and increases crash risk; distracted driving is unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your steering wheel?
options: a:Signal and keep the wheels turned left.,b:Signal and keep the wheels straight while waiting.,c:Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you turn.
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to make a left turn. If you are rear-ended, straight wheels prevent being pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: When is it illegal to cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When crossing would interfere with other traffic.,b:When turning left into a private driveway.,c:When the car in front of you is disabled.
note: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes only if you can do so safely and without interfering with traffic.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,b:Just set the parking brake.,c:Leave the engine running if it's cold out.
note: When leaving an unattended vehicle you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in school zones?
options: a:10 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:30 mph.
note: Unless another speed is posted, the speed limit in school zones is 20 mph; drive cautiously near schools.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what is required?
options: a:Slow down until it passes.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
note: Yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights or siren by immediately driving to the right and stopping until it has passed.

question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It has no effect on either.,d:It only affects judgment at very high doses.
note: Alcohol impairs vision, reaction time, judgment, and increases risk-taking; it harms both skills and judgment needed for safe driving.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching using siren and/or lights, what must you do immediately?
