options: a:Pull to the right and slow down but stay in your lane.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and continue driving.,c:Pull to the right and stop.
note: When approached by an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes.

question: Where is it unlawful to park?
options: a:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,b:Anywhere on a hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: You may not park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parallel parking on the street, be within 12 inches of the curb.

question: What may reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Ignoring posted speed limits.,b:Speeding to get ahead of other drivers.,c:Allowing extra travel time and using proper signals.,d:Yelling at drivers who cut you off.
note: Allowing extra travel time, obeying speed limits, and signaling properly can help reduce incidents of road rage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To make a left turn from a multilane, one-way street onto another one-way street, where should you start your turn?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The nearest bicycle lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.,d:The left lane.
note: To turn left from a multilane, one-way street, begin from the left lane and complete the turn into the left lane of the street you enter.

question: How should a lap belt be positioned for proper restraint?
options: a:Loose across the stomach.,b:Snugly across your hip bones and the lower abdomen.,c:Hidden beneath the seat cushion.,d:Across your neck for support.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across the hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should lie comfortably across the chest.

question: If you drive through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to do what?
options: a:Know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Potentially run out into the street without looking.
note: Children may not recognize traffic dangers and could run into the roadway without looking; reduce speed and be prepared to stop.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, you should allow a larger space cushion because:
options: a:There is more oncoming traffic uphill.,b:It is easier to stop on an incline.,c:The vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic starts moving again.
note: Leave more space when stopped on an uphill so if the car ahead rolls back it won't hit your vehicle.

question: After a collision, which action should drivers take at or near the scene?
options: a:Drive away if no one appears injured.,b:Stand or walk in traffic lanes to inspect damage.,c:Stop the vehicle at or near the scene.,d:Leave the ignitions of wrecked vehicles on.
note: You must stop at or near the scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and turn off ignitions of damaged vehicles.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by what color lines?
options: a:White lines.,b:Yellow lines.,c:Red lines.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; yellow separates opposing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit on a highway outside thickly settled areas and business districts is:
options: a:20 mph.,b:50 mph (do not exceed this under normal conditions).,c:10 mph.
note: Unless otherwise posted, the normal maximum for such highways is 50 mph; you must drive slower when conditions require.

question: If another driver behaves aggressively toward you, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating.,b:Get out of your vehicle to confront them.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.,d:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
note: When faced with aggressive driving, stay calm, avoid eye contact, put distance between vehicles, slow down, and allow them to pass safely.

question: When following a heavy truck uphill, you should know:
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed and you may not be able to pass safely on a hill.,b:The truck will always keep the posted speed limit.,c:It is always legal to pass on a hill if you have room.
note: Large trucks often slow on inclines; visibility and legality issues can make passing unsafe on hills.

question: When a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon shows a solid yellow light, you must:
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop.,b:Come to a complete stop immediately.,c:Proceed without change.
note: A solid yellow PHB light warns drivers to slow and be prepared to stop for pedestrians.

question: Bicycles on the road are considered:
options: a:Vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.,b:Obstructions that must always yield to cars.,c:Non-traffic objects.
note: Cyclists have the same rights and duties as drivers; motorists should respect bicyclists' legal status.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed only if the bus driver waves you on.,b:Pass slowly if you think children are clear.,c:Honk before passing on the left.,d:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, all traffic in both directions (in most situations) must stop until children are safe and the arm is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.,b:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the left has the right-of-way at all times.,d:The largest vehicle has right-of-way.
note: At an all-way stop the first vehicle to reach and stop at the intersection goes first; if two arrive together, the driver on the right goes first.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To warn others in hazardous situations, such as a child about to run into the street.,b:To greet a friend at an intersection.,c:While passing a bicyclist.
note: Use the horn as a warning when another road user may not see you and a collision is possible.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only use the outside mirrors.
note: Always turn your head to check blind spots in addition to using mirrors before every lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign at an intersection, how should you check traffic before proceeding?
options: a:Look only forward and go when clear.,b:Look left first, then right, then left again.,c:Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.,d:Check your rearview mirror then go.
note: When stopped you should scan the intersection carefully: look left, then right, then left again to ensure the way is clear before proceeding.

question: Your chances of being in a collision start to rise after consuming how many alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Only after four or more drinks.,b:After three or more drinks only.,c:Even after one drink your crash risk is higher.
note: Alcohol increases crash risk even at low levels; no one can drink and drive safely.

question: While driving on a divided multilane highway you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are free.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Slow down, move to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop when safe.,d:Speed up to clear the way.
note: If you hear sirens or see flashing lights, move aside to give emergency vehicles a clear path and stop; do not attempt to outrun them.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your seat so you can see and reach controls properly.,b:Your rearview mirror only.,c:Your steering wheel only.
note: Adjust the seat first to ensure comfortable position and clear visibility; then set mirrors and steering wheel if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, what should you do?
options: a:You have the right-of-way.,b:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,c:Force your way into traffic if necessary.,d:Stop only if traffic is heavy.
note: Drivers entering roadways from private property must yield to traffic already on the public road and merge when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it unsafe or unlawful to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On a hill or curve, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.,b:Only when a police officer is present.,c:When the vehicle ahead is traveling below the speed limit.,d:When the passing lane is empty.
note: Do not pass on hills or curves, at intersections, before or on railroad crossings, over bridges, or where signs prohibit passing.

question: If someone is tailgating you and there is an open lane to your right, you should:
options: a:Move over to the right lane if it is safe to do so.,b:Gradually reduce your speed immediately to force them to back off.,c:Brake suddenly to make them stop following you.
note: If you're being tailgated and a right lane is open, safely move right to let the tailgater pass. If you cannot change lanes, slow down gradually to encourage them to pass. Never brake abruptly.

question: Which factor never affects a vehicle's stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,d:The condition and type of the road surface.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, speed, vehicle condition, tire condition, roadway surface, weather, and visibility—not the time of day per se.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when you meet oncoming traffic, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop always.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over.
note: On narrow roads both drivers should leave adequate space; yield at least half the traveled portion to oncoming traffic.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:When lights have stopped flashing.,c:When the train has already passed.,d:If the crossing is not busy.
note: You must never go around lowered railroad crossing gates; always obey signals, lights, and flaggers for safety.

question: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means:
options: a:Speed limit.,b:Stop.,c:Hospital ahead.
note: An eight-sided sign is always a stop sign; you must come to a complete stop when approaching it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it required to use your turn signal?
options: a:When changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley/parking area.,b:Only when turning left.,c:Only when turning onto another street.
note: Always use the proper signal to communicate lane changes, parking maneuvers, and when entering traffic from an alley or parking area.

question: What should you do just before changing lanes?
options: a:Quickly turn your head without checking mirrors.,b:Check your side and rearview mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,c:Only use your signal without checking behind you.,d:Signal after you begin the lane change.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder to ensure there are no vehicles in your blind spot.

question: A solid white edge line that slants toward the left indicates:
options: a:The road is narrowing ahead.,b:An intersection is coming up.,c:A construction zone immediately ahead.
note: If the right edge line angles toward the center, the roadway narrows ahead.

question: If you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.,b:Proceed without stopping if no other vehicles are present.,c:Come to a full stop, yield as required, and proceed when it is safe.
note: A flashing red traffic light acts like a stop sign: you must stop, yield the right-of-way, and proceed when safe.

question: Which of the following can impair driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol, any medication, or lack of sleep.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only alcohol.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness; all affect safe driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on major highways, what should you do to avoid 'highway hypnosis' and be prepared for hazards?
options: a:Stay alert and avoid staring at any one thing for more than a few seconds.,b:Keep your eyes fixed on the center of the road at all times.,c:Turn off your headlights in bright daylight.
note: Avoid highway hypnosis by keeping your eyes moving and staying alert so you can react to unexpected hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the left side mirror.,b:Glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Only look in the rearview mirror.
note: To check your blind spot, turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move to ensure no vehicle is there.

question: What should you do on slippery roads?
options: a:Drive more quickly to pass hazardous patches.,b:Use cruise control for steady speed.,c:Slow down.,d:Maintain the posted speed limit no matter what.
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet; driving slower than the posted speed may be necessary for safety.

question: When passing on a multilane highway, you must:
options: a:Ensure the passing lane is clear and signal before changing lanes.,b:Always pass only on the right.,c:Watch for oncoming traffic in the opposite direction.
note: Make sure the passing lane is clear, signal, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: When sharing the road with a motorcycle, what must you allow the motorcyclist?
options: a:The use of a complete lane.,b:The use of half a lane only.,c:The use of the shoulder alongside your vehicle.
note: A motorcycle is entitled to the full width of a lane. Do not try to share the lane with a motorcyclist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Do not pass from your lane.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down immediately.
note: A solid yellow adjacent to your lane means passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: If a fire engine is following you but not using its emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving normally; you do not need to clear a path.,b:Pull over and stop immediately.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If an emergency vehicle is following but not using siren or lights, you do not need to clear the path; continue driving normally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: High speeds affect crashes by:
options: a:Greatly increasing stopping distances and severity of collisions.,b:Decreasing stopping distances.,c:Having no effect on crash severity.
note: Higher speeds increase the distance needed to stop and the severity of impacts in a collision.

question: When you hear a siren from an emergency vehicle behind you while driving, you should:
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop or, in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can safely get out of the way.,b:Stop immediately where you are.,c:Speed up to get away.
note: Create a clear path for the emergency vehicle by safely pulling over to the side; in heavy traffic keep moving slowly until you can yield.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:Only if you confirm a train is not close.,b:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,c:Never drive around or under a gate that is moving up or down.
note: Flashing lights, lowered gates, and bells mean you must stop. Do not go across the tracks until the gates are fully raised, lights and bells stop, and it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway safely you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to freeway traffic, and merge at about the same speed traffic is moving.,b:Signal and expect freeway traffic to yield to you.,c:Enter slowly and stop if necessary.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, signal, and yield to traffic already on the freeway.

question: What does a steady green light at an intersection mean?
options: a:You may drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,b:You must slow and prepare to stop.,c:You must stop and check for oncoming traffic.,d:You must yield to all turning vehicles.
note: A steady green signal allows you to proceed through the intersection when it is safe; you must still yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what is the best action to take?
options: a:Get some coffee and continue driving.,b:Open the window and keep driving.,c:Stop driving and rest or change drivers.,d:Turn up the radio and drive faster.
note: Driving while fatigued is dangerous; stop driving, rest, or change drivers rather than continuing while drowsy.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition is passing another vehicle permitted?
options: a:When you are on a hill or in a curve because the view is usually clear.,b:By driving onto the shoulder of the road.,c:When the center line next to your lane is a broken yellow line and the passing lane ahead is clear.,d:Across a solid yellow line whenever traffic is light.
note: You may pass only where allowed by pavement markings; a broken yellow line next to your lane means passing is permitted when it is safe and clear ahead.

question: As alcohol levels in your blood increase, what effect occurs?
options: a:Your reaction time slows down.,b:You become less confident.,c:The alcohol metabolizes itself faster.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, impairs judgment, reduces concentration, and makes drivers overconfident and more error-prone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working signals, which should drivers obey?
options: a:The traffic signal lights only.,b:The directions given by the officer.,c:Honking to alert the officer.,d:Traffic signs posted nearby rather than the officer's directions.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their instructions override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's directions for safe traffic flow.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady green arrow, drivers:
options: a:May turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Must stop and wait for a solid green light.,c:Should treat it as a caution and merge into that lane.
note: A green arrow permits the indicated turn; you must be in the proper lane and yield to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a highway, you should:
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic and merge into a gap.,b:Enter far below highway speed and expect others to adjust.,c:Stop at the ramp end and then enter slowly.
note: Acceleration lanes allow you to match highway speed and merge safely into traffic; always signal and yield.

question: What should a driver do after taking an over-the-counter medication before driving?
options: a:Double the dose to stay alert.,b:Drink alcohol to offset side effects.,c:Read the medication label for warnings about driving.,d:Ignore the label and drive as usual.
note: Many non-prescription drugs can affect driving ability. Read labels for warnings and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure.

question: What is a good general rule about passing other vehicles?
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible.,b:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic to improve visibility.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and safe.
note: Each pass increases collision risk; stay with traffic speed and pass only as needed and legal.

question: When driving in fog you should use which lights?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow to reduce glare and improve visibility.

question: If another driver cuts you off, the safest response is to:
options: a:Let it go and continue driving safely.,b:Pull next to them and shout.,c:Flash your high beams at them.
note: To avoid road rage and reduce crash risk, do not take it personally; let it go and keep driving safely.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Red lines.,b:Yellow lines.,c:Black lines.,d:White lines.
note: Yellow lines divide lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

question: Which of the following is a common source of distracted driving?
options: a:Checking tire pressure while driving.,b:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,c:Changing the oil before driving.
note: Many actions, like eating, drinking, smoking, texting, or adjusting the radio, distract drivers and increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which of the following?
options: a:The maximum posted speed limit only.,b:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for conditions.,c:A speed that is safe for existing conditions regardless of posted limits.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for the current conditions, which may be lower than the posted limit when necessary.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive and may result in DUII?
options: a:Alcoholic beverages such as beer, wine, or liquor.,b:Controlled substances and certain prescription medicines.,c:Inhalants such as glue or paint.,d:All of the above.
note: A wide range of intoxicants—alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some legal medications—can impair driving and lead to arrest for DUII.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign indicates:
options: a:A road hazard or warning.,b:An interstate route.,c:A school crossing.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs that alert drivers to hazards or special road conditions ahead.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Assume it operates like any other vehicle.,b:Hide defects from the owner to avoid embarrassment.,c:Take a few minutes to locate and test the controls and check for defects.
note: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, familiarize yourself with the location and operation of lights, wipers, brakes, signals, gear selector, and horn. Correct any defects first.

question: When should you slow down?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads.,b:Only when a police officer tells you to.,c:Only when passing another vehicle.
note: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, railroad crossings, steep hills, blind curves, and when the road is wet or slippery.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, or before entering the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed if clear.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are present.
note: You must stop at the designated stop line, before any crosswalk, or before entering the intersection on a red light.

question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, you should:
options: a:Stop for a rest every two hours.,b:Drive faster to finish earlier.,c:Do arm exercises while driving.
note: On long trips, stop every two hours for a break; if drowsy, park safely and rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space required to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:Whether a stop sign is present.,c:Whether you have signaled.
note: The space you need to cross depends on road and weather conditions and the speed and distance of oncoming traffic.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,b:Always stop whether a stop sign is present or not.,c:Sound your horn to alert children.
note: Always be alert for children near school crossings and be prepared to stop for pedestrians.

question: Which of the following about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:You should check antifreeze and washer fluid levels more often.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,d:Snow tires can increase traction on slippery surfaces.
note: Do not use cruise control on snow, in rain, or in similar hazardous conditions; winter driving requires extra precautions and preparation.

question: What best ensures safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Honk your horn before shifting to reverse.,b:Check behind the vehicle by walking to the rear before getting in the driver's seat.,c:Rely only on rearview mirrors and cameras.,d:Back quickly to finish sooner.
note: Before backing, walk around and inspect the area behind the vehicle for children or obstacles rather than relying solely on mirrors.

question: What color lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:White lines.,c:Green lines.,d:Blue lines.
note: Yellow center lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions; broken or solid patterns indicate passing rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:You yes,b:No,c:Yes
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing; you may only cross to turn into/from a driveway or make a permitted left turn.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive faster through standing water.,b:Drive through shallow water only.,c:Drive more slowly in wet conditions.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet roads; reduce speed to lower the chance of losing traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a green light change to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Ignore it and continue at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow warns the signal is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed carefully.

question: Anything that causes you to which of the following could lead to a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road.,b:Take your hands off the wheel.,c:Take your attention away from the task of driving.
note: Any activity that diverts your attention, eyes, or hands from driving is a distraction and increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are drivers permitted to text while operating a motor vehicle?
options: a:Yes,b:No,c:You yes,d:Only when parked on the shoulder.
note: You may not write, send, or read electronic messages while driving. This includes texts, emails, and internet use.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow displayed at an intersection mean?
options: a:The green arrow is coming next so speed up.,b:You may proceed in the arrow direction without yielding.,c:Slow to a stop if you can do so safely because a red arrow is coming.,d:The signal is malfunctioning.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected-turn indication is ending; stop if it is safe to do so since a red arrow will follow.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,c:Passing is permitted from either lane.
note: When a broken yellow is beside a solid yellow, only the side with the broken line may pass when safe.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving skills?
options: a:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can limit concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.,b:Only a BAC above the legal limit impairs driving.,c:Alcohol does not affect driving at low doses.
note: Any amount of alcohol reduces mental and physical skills needed for safe driving.

question: If another driver aggressively cuts you off, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights to show them they were wrong.,b:Call the police right away.,c:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, remain calm and get out of their way. Attempting to retaliate increases danger and may escalate the situation.

question: Drowsy drivers may:
options: a:Safely continue by drinking coffee.,b:Drive so poorly they resemble intoxicated drivers.,c:Stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
note: Drowsiness can impair driving similar to alcohol; opening windows or coffee are not reliable fixes—stop and rest if drowsy.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always signal when which of the following actions is performed?
options: a:Only when parking at night.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Only when other vehicles are present.
note: Always use your signals when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area.

question: Signs colored orange typically indicate what?
options: a:School zone signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Work zone signs.
note: Orange signs are used in highway work zones to warn of construction and related hazards.

question: A red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection indicates:
options: a:Decrease speed and yield the right-of-way to others.,b:Stop completely under all circumstances.,c:Always stop and honk before proceeding.
note: A red-and-white triangular sign is a yield sign: slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield to traffic or pedestrians as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline marking?
options: a:A single broken yellow line.,b:A combination solid and broken yellow line.,c:A double solid yellow line.,d:A dashed white line.
note: A double solid yellow centerline on a two-way road indicates that passing is prohibited from either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in traffic, the safest practice is to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic rather than much faster or slower than others.,b:Drive much faster than surrounding traffic to avoid congestion.,c:Drive much slower than others to be safer.
note: Crashes often occur when speeds differ significantly between vehicles; keep pace with traffic within the speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must drivers do when approaching a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Drive through if no other traffic is present.,b:Come to a complete stop and then proceed only as permitted.,c:Speed through to clear the intersection quickly.,d:Ignore it if turning is allowed without signage.
note: A steady red light means stop. You may turn on red only where legal and after yielding to pedestrians and other traffic, unless a sign prohibits it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To change lanes safely, what sequence should you follow?
options: a:Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes without looking over your shoulder.,b:Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder, then change lanes.,c:Signal and change lanes immediately.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check the blind spot, and change lanes only when it is safe.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, look for a train, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to beat any approaching train.,c:Drive around any lowered gate if traffic backs up.,d:Ignore unmarked crossings.
note: When you see signs for a nearby railroad crossing, reduce speed, look and listen for trains, and stop if warning devices activate or a train is near.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look to avoid being blinded?
options: a:Directly at the headlights.,b:Toward the left side of the road.,c:Toward the right side of the road.,d:At the center line.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams while keeping enough view of the roadway to stay on course.

question: When must you turn on your headlights in Massachusetts tunnels?
options: a:Only during nighttime hours.,b:Only if visibility is poor.,c:Always when driving in a tunnel.
note: Massachusetts law requires headlights to be on when driving in tunnels to increase visibility for yourself and others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you go through an intersection controlled by a stop sign but there is no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After slowing down and checking there is no cross traffic.,b:Only after coming to a full stop before entering the intersection and verifying it is safe to proceed.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
note: If a stop sign controls an intersection but there is no stop line or crosswalk, come to a complete stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when it is safe.

question: A bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws:
options: a:Can be ticketed just like a motor vehicle driver.,b:Has special immunity and cannot be ticketed.,c:Will always be warned but not cited.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as motor vehicle drivers and can be cited for violations.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should steer:
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid and hold it.,c:Keep the front wheels straight at all costs.
note: If you skid, steer toward the direction you want the vehicle to travel; when it straightens, correct as needed.

question: Which is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Using turn signals properly.,b:Keeping a steady following distance.,c:Driving exactly at the speed limit.,d:Weaving between lanes.
note: Telltale signs of impairment include weaving, erratic speed changes, sudden stops, and jerking motions; stay away and report if safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is using your horn appropriate?
options: a:When passing another car.,b:To alert others when you must stop quickly.,c:Whenever you are frustrated with another driver.
note: Sound your horn to warn others of immediate danger or if you lose control and need to alert nearby drivers; do not use it aggressively.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Exit at the next exit and safely return to your intended exit.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the interstate.,c:Roll down your window and ask another driver for directions.
note: Do not back up or turn around on the highway. Continue to the next exit and re-route safely.

question: Regulatory signs are usually what color and must be obeyed?
options: a:White.,b:Blue.,c:Green.
note: Regulatory signs typically have a white background with black or red markings and must always be obeyed.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:No,b:Yes,c:You yes
note: It is against the law to consume or possess open alcoholic beverages on public roads; open containers in areas normally occupied by driver or passenger are prohibited.

question: “Highway hypnosis” is most likely caused by:
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods without actively scanning.,b:Taking frequent rest stops.,c:Getting too much sleep before the trip.,d:Listening to loud music.
note: Highway hypnosis results from staring ahead for long periods and not actively scanning; take breaks and shift your gaze to stay alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed and turn.,b:Yield to pedestrians and any traffic in the intersection.,c:Stop only if a police officer is present.,d:Signal after you start the turn.
note: Turning on a green light requires yielding to pedestrians and other traffic already in the intersection unless a sign prohibits the turn.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Never pass trucks or buses.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,c:Flash your headlights at them to get their attention.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots; do not drive alongside them and avoid following too closely so the driver can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway you should begin slowing:
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road before the exit lane.,c:Only when you see the toll booth.
note: Do not slow on the main roadway; move into the exit lane and then reduce speed on the exit ramp.

question: When a flagger is controlling traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Ignore the flagger and follow other drivers.,b:Assume the flagger isn't authorized to direct traffic.,c:Follow the flagger's directions.
note: Be prepared to slow and use caution when directed by signs, a flagger, or law enforcement. Ignoring a flagger is illegal and dangerous in construction zones.

question: The act of turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:A good driving habit.,c:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.,d:Only required for new drivers.
note: Checking your blind spot by turning your head is a proper habit to ensure the lane you intend to enter is clear of vehicles or bicycles.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach.,b:Body weight of the individual.,c:How much time passes between drinks.,d:All of the above.
note: BAC and impairment depend on amount consumed, time between drinks, body weight, and whether food was eaten, among other factors.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:You are traveling much faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic might not see you pull out to pass the bicyclist.
note: When passing bicycles, be cautious because cyclists may swerve to avoid obstacles, and oncoming traffic might not see you move into the lane to pass.

question: Which of the following will help you sober up quickly after drinking?
options: a:A cold shower.,b:A large coffee.,c:Exercising.,d:None of the above; only time will sober you.
note: There is no quick way to remove alcohol from your system; only time allows your body to metabolize it.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and no passing is allowed.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and can be crossed when safe to pass.

question: About speed management when navigating curves, you should:
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve.,b:Maintain posted speed until the sharpest part, then slow.,c:Accelerate gently into the curve.
note: Because inertia affects control, reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain steerability.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The medicine will block the alcohol's effects.,b:Alcohol will help the medicine work faster.,c:The combination can multiply the impairing effects of both substances.
note: Combining alcohol with medications can multiply the impairing effects, sometimes producing far greater impairment than alcohol alone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While in a travel lane on the roadway, which is true?
options: a:You may stop briefly to drop off passengers.,b:You should keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.,c:You may make a U-turn if you missed an entrance ramp.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane. If you miss a turn or exit, continue to the next safe location to turn around or exit. Never back up in a travel lane.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Because visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Cars overheat more often at night.,c:It rains more at night.
note: Reduced vision at night shrinks your field of view; adjust speed and use proper headlights to stop within visible distance.

question: If you are in a serious motor vehicle crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Ignore the scene and continue driving.,b:Drive away if the damage seems minor.,c:Argue with the other driver before exchanging information.,d:Determine if anyone is injured and call emergency services if needed.
note: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible, check for injuries, call 911 if anyone is hurt, and report crashes when required by law.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and keep driving.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit.
note: On a one-way street, drive toward the nearest roadside and stop when an emergency vehicle using lights or sirens approaches.

question: When driving in fog, you should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams and fog lights if available; high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

question: Which actions should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Signal your lane change only.,b:Check your rearview and outside mirrors only.,c:Check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,d:Change lanes without signaling if you can do it quickly.
note: When changing lanes you must signal, check all mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.

question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Move the injured person immediately to clear traffic.,b:Always leave the injured where they are and wait.,c:Avoid moving the injured unless necessary, keep them warm, and give first aid if trained.
note: Do not move injured persons unnecessarily; untrained handling can worsen injuries. Keep the injured warm and provide first aid if needed until professional help arrives.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:Only during daytime.,b:On hills and curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.,c:Only when pavement is wet.,d:Only in school zones.
note: Passing is unsafe and often illegal on hills, curves, intersections, railroad crossings, and where signs prohibit it.

question: What should you remember about wet pavement and rain?
options: a:Wet roads cannot cause hydroplaning.,b:You should always tailgate to increase control.,c:Pavement is especially slippery right after rain begins.
note: Road surfaces are often most slippery immediately after rainfall because oil and dirt mix with the water; reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: You are in the left lane and want to move right. Before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Check mirrors,b:Look in mirrors,c:Only signal and change lanes without checking blind spots.
note: When changing lanes to the right, glance over your right shoulder plus check mirrors and signal to ensure the lane is clear.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when which of the following occurs?
options: a:Directed to do so by a flagger.,b:The crossing is controlled by a stop sign.,c:Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.
note: Stop at a crossing when flashing red signals or lowered gates indicate an approaching train; also when directed by a flagger or stop sign.

question: Which statement about advisory speed signs on curves is correct?
options: a:They are blue with black lettering.,b:You should reduce speed before entering the curve as indicated.,c:They can be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.,d:They are triangular in shape.
note: Advisory speed signs attached to curve warnings show a recommended safe speed. Slow before entering the curve; do not rely on braking while turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually best practice?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights until fully merged.,b:Proceed slowly and wait for an opening at low speed.,c:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic and blend in.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic on the freeway so you can merge safely without disrupting flow.

question: Which action is illegal at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Stopping when directed by a flagger.,b:Waiting for a train to pass.,c:Driving around lowered gates.,d:Obeying flashing lights and gates.
note: You must obey flashing lights, gates, and flaggers; it is illegal and dangerous to go around lowered crossing gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the right.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle that honks first.
note: At an intersection of equal roads without signs or signals, yield to the vehicle approaching from your right.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement indicates that drivers in that lane:
options: a:May choose to make the movement but are not required to.,b:Must make the movement shown by the arrow.,c:Must stop before making the movement.,d:Should yield to traffic in the oncoming lane.
note: Pavement arrows indicate the required movement from that lane; follow any signs or signals that apply first.

question: What is the purpose of regulatory road signs?
options: a:They warn of present dangers ahead.,b:They indicate what a driver must or must not do.,c:They are always diamond-shaped and yellow or green.,d:They show nearby services and distances.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what actions are required or prohibited in a given area, such as speed limits, no turns, or lane usage.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Ignore the signal and continue normally.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means caution. Slow down, look carefully, and proceed with care if the way is clear.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:When the bus is stopped and its red lights are flashing.,b:Only when the bus is in your lane and doors are open.,c:Only if the bus driver signals you to stop.
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights and/or extends its stop arm.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving much slower than the speed limit and causing backup, what should you do?
options: a:Continue at the slow speed because it is safest.,b:Always expect the right-of-way.,c:Pull off the road when safe to allow other vehicles to pass.
note: Driving well below the flow of traffic can be hazardous; if you are causing a backup, you are required to pull off the road and let other vehicles pass.

question: If you encounter an animal on the roadway, what is the safest response?
options: a:Take no special action and continue.,b:Slow down and pass the animal carefully to avoid startling it.,c:Pass the animal as closely as possible to get by quickly.
note: Be very cautious when animals are on the road; slow down and pass slowly to avoid startling them and causing unpredictable behavior.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway divided by double solid yellow lines, you may:
options: a:Cross only to make a left turn into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross to pass another vehicle when no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Never cross under any circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them only to make permitted left turns into driveways, alleys, or business entrances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic near a school, what must you do?
options: a:Ignore the guard if a traffic signal is present.,b:Assume the guard is not authorized to direct traffic.,c:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,d:Do whatever surrounding traffic does even if it contradicts the guard.
note: Drivers must obey directions from crossing guards in school zones and exercise extra caution, reducing speed when instructed.
